# The Most Enduring Piece of 9/11 Art? A Musical Set in Canada.

“Come From Away,” about a remote Newfoundland community that embraced grounded travelers, is playing all over the world — even in the town where it takes place.

# The Most Enduring Piece of 9/11 Art? A Musical Set in Canada.

“Come From Away,” about a remote Newfoundland community that embraced grounded travelers, is playing all over the world — even in the town where it takes place.

Credit...

Supported by

By Michael Paulson [...] By Michael Paulson

Visuals by Johnny C.Y. Lam

Michael Paulson has seen “Come From Away” 10 times over 10 years. He reported this article from Gander, Newfoundland, a decade after his first reporting trip there.

In the quarter century since the terrorist attacks of Sept. 11, 2001, the horror of that day has inspired novels, films, television shows, paintings and sculpture. [...] But the most enduring artistic response has been an uplifting Canadian musical, “Come From Away,” about a small town with a big airport where nearly 7,000 travelers were diverted amid the chaos and fear.

results.title: 9/11’s Dust and Ash Coated Their Childhood. Is It Still Making Them Ill?
results.content:
When the south tower collapsed that morning, Sept. 11, 2001, the windows of their apartment blew in. Dust and debris filled their home, bringing darkness. Sarah thought a monster had come for them.

Their mother and nanny carried them and their 2-year-old sister into a stairwell frantic with fleeing neighbors, then down to a basement boiler room. Someone distributed strips of wet fabric, with instructions to breathe through it as a filter. [...] Jacob Fortinsky and his twin sister, Sarah, were a month away from turning 4 when the first jetliner slammed into the World Trade Center 25 years ago. They had been watching Franklin the Turtle cartoons in their apartment one block west, on the 21st floor of Gateway Plaza. As fire trucks and ambulances gathered below, the twins began to count them.
